images.seen: Start anchor reads right: Roman Empire, Sasanian Empire, Western Jin, Gupta-era India split into small states; no stray cells.
End of window reads right: Western and Eastern Roman Empires, Huns on the Pontic steppe, Gupta and Western Satraps, Later Yan/Later Qin/Northern Wei split of the north, Cuan clan in Yunnan.
Europe and Near East: Illyricum line between the two Roman halves sits near the Drina and Sava; Armenia split drawn as Sasanian vassal tint plus a small Roman share; nothing far out of place.

Hole of nobody's land round Chang'an inside Han-Zhao and Jin land (Jin keyframe lacks Guanzhong), plus a grey patch at Hanzhong; patched for Guanzhong, Chongqing and the Ning Province corners; Hanzhong left.

India: Gupta direct on the Ganges with the Rajasthan, Punjab and Sind tributary tint, Yaudheya inside, Vakataka, Kadamba, Kalabhra, Western Satraps, Kidarites at the Hindu Kush: matches the dossiers; compiled and Cliopatria agree on the outline.

Sixteen Kingdoms in 386: Later Qin, Western Yan, Later Yan, Western Qin, Later Liang, Northern Wei belt, Former Qin contested; where Cliopatria draws one Former Qin the dossiers split it. Nobody discs at Luoyang (385-389, 150 cells) and a Later Qin/Former Qin ring at Chang'an; not patched.

Huns reach the Carpathians (Gothia gone by dossier ledger 375-376), Gothic War zone striped in Thrace and Moesia, Caucasus kingdoms and Lazica drawn; matches the Huns and Gothia ledgers though Cliopatria still shows Gothia.
Nubia and Red Sea: Nobatia, Makuria, Alodia, Axum, Himyar, Lakhmid as Sasanian vassal; consistent with Cliopatria except for Axum's Yemen piece, which the dossiers do not draw.
After the patch: Guanzhong is Jin land again, Hanzhong still a grey patch (pages silent), Dai and Former Zhao as designed.

issues.what: Land held by nobody 306-316 that the pages put under Jin: the Wei valley round Chang'an (Jin's capital 312-316), Chongqing to 310 and the Yunnan/Guizhou corners of Ning Province to 333. The cheng-han and former-zhao dossiers cut these out of Cliopatria's Cheng Han and Former Zhao shapes, but the Jin keyframes are Cliopatria's shapes as drawn, which lack them too. About 420 cells of nobody's land at 308-312 are now Jin's.

Gupta tributary land (Rajasthan, Punjab, Sind and the Eastern Kushan frontier, 2,245 cells) is unowned 380-382: the dossier's own 380 vassal_end draws it direct but the compiler leaves a vassal_end's land to nobody until the 383 keyframe snap. The 383 snap of 2,254 cells is gone.

Kingdom of Kucha (-150..648) owns no cell at any anchor from 100 on: the Western Regions colony takes its land by the colony rule. Kucha has its own kings in the period and falls only in 383 to Lu Guang; the protectorate is revived by Former Liang only in 335. Kucha is drawn independent 300-334 (about 240 cells).

Kutai Martadipura (399-1635, the earliest Hindu kingdom of the East Indies) has no land: its shape names Muara Kaman and Kutai Lama, places the gazetteer does not know. Drawn as a 30 km disc round Muara Kaman (the dossier's capital coordinates) plus the Mahakam outline of Cliopatria's Kutai 1648 shape (41 cells).

cuan-clan against western-jin, 5,137 cell-years in Yunnan, won by the smaller Cuan. The Cuanman page calls the regime 'local and semi-independent' and gives no Jin appointment; a vassal ruling would be a reading of 'semi-independent', and Cheng-Han also claimed Ning Province from 333.

Hanzhong (79 cells, lat 32.3-33.3, lon 106-108) is nobody's 306-313: cut from Cheng's 306 shape (Cheng's from 314) but no keyframe gives it to Jin. The Cheng-Han page says only that 'rebelling refugees in Hanzhong surrendered the region to Cheng' in 314 and not who held it.

Sixteen Kingdoms keyframe snaps (former-zhao_311 2,292 cells, later-zhao_319 1,508 removed, former-zhao_306 1,212 removed, later-yan_384 1,040 removed, southern-yan_398 827 removed, former-yan_353) are the dossiers' own design: the keyframe is narrower than the ledger gain and the land comes back a few years later (Former Zhao 306-310 about 1,000 cells nobody's; Later Zhao 319-322 about 660 cells in Shandong, Cao Ni's land; Later Yan 384, Southern Yan 398 one year). No page opened settles who held the gaps.

The Western Regions: western-jin ledger/24 releases 3,456 cells of 'Tarim city-states' to nobody in 328, and the protectorate (2,088 cells at 399) stays drawn in Western Jin's tint to 399, although the Protectorate page says it was revived in 335 by Former Liang. No dossier exists for the Tarim states other than Kucha (kingdom-of-khotan starts 851).

Large flagged conflicts that the smaller state rightly won or that match the dossiers: alemanni/roman-empire (Agri Decumates), sasanian-empire/xionites (Sogdia), later-yan/northern-wei 394-397, mahameghavahana/vakataka and nagas/vakataka in the Deccan, gupta/vakataka 347. Domain of Magnus Maximus (383-388, 6,644 cells at its end) matches its ledger (Britain, Gaul, Spain, then Italy in 387).

Duplicate dossiers for one state: san-marino (301-2026, with the ledger 1320 and 1463 and keyframes 301-1462, 1463-2026) and republic-of-san-marino (301-2026, keyframes 1797 and 1799). Both found at 301 on the same cell; only the Republic's dossier owns it.

dossier_requests.what: merge with republic-of-san-marino (one state, two dossiers); keep the richer ledger of san-marino and the Cliopatria name of the Republic
dossier_requests.why: The page says San Marino is 'officially the Republic of San Marino', founded 3 September 301 (traditional). Both dossiers found it on 301 on the same cell, so the second is dropped and its keyframes (1797, 1799) and ledger (1320, 1463 gains) are inconsistent with the first.

problems: hierarchy: data/colonies.csv row protectorate-of-the-western-regions,western-jin,267,420 (confidence high) draws the protectorate (2,088 cells at 399) in Western Jin's tint to 399. The Protectorate page: 'The protectorate was again revived in 335 by [Former Liang] and headquartered in [Gaochang] until the demise of [Northern Liang]' (439), so from 335 its metropole is Former Liang and its successors, not Western Jin; the row should end in 334 or be re-split at 335 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protectorate_of_the_Western_Regions).

Side effect of keyframe_overrides/0,1,3,4: the 'wrong' keyframe western-jin_324 (the 337 shape, which lacks the Yunnan/Guizhou corners) now releases 206 cells to nobody at 324, a new snap in the trial; the cells were nobody's from 306 before, and are Jin's 306-323 now. The Li Xiong page puts them in Jin's Ning Province until Li Shou's capture in 333; extending Jin to 332 and giving Cheng-Han the land in 333 needs a further override of western-jin_317 and an event, left undone.

keyframe_overrides/2 replaces the single keyframe kutai-martadipura_399 that runs 399-1634 (other windows): the outline may overlap the later kutai-kingdom (from 1300, the Kutai Lama core) and be settled there by the size rule; the dossier calls the outline an over-cover for the 4th century. The p1300-p1599 and p1600 window agents may see a new conflict pair.
The Kucha ruling and event leave 1 cell of Kucha after 335 (the protectorate's 335 gain region is Cliopatria's protectorate shape); harmless.

Not examined for lack of pages: Mesoamerica (mayan-city-states is a 1,340-cell Cliopatria aggregate while tikal holds 3 cells, caracol 5, teotihuacan 40), Northern Wei's 386-395 shape (the dossier calls the Cliopatria 387 shape of 320,631 km2, 28 % Hebei, unverified), the Luoyang/Henan hole 385-389 (153 cells) and Khwarezm released by the Sasanians at 306 (373 cells, the dossier says no page dates it).
The first WebFetch of https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuan_clan failed (url_not_found); the Cuanman page was used instead and counted once.

The trial of the real patch file ran clean: 8 entries applied, rulings/0 settled 201 cell-years, the gupta-empire_383 snap and the western-jin_311 snap vanished; the end anchor p0400 differs from the published one in 53 cells (38 Kutai, the rest Gupta/Satraps/Sasanian border cells from the 380 gain).
